matthewmcg
i've worked on projects when we had both c and c++. i don't want to be
confused here.

from a developer perspective, c++ makes it much easier to write good code.

from a maintainer's perspective, c++ made it easier for you to write good
code, when the compiler was on our side. it was a huge time saver from a
maintainer perspective.

this doesn't mean that c++ was perfect, by any means. it does mean that there
are lots of bugs in c++, that c and c++ are not as good as each other, and the
code is not as good as it could be, but it also means that the code is as good
as it could be.

in my opinion, the maintainers and developers of the project were equally
well aware of the issues, they just didn't communicate them clearly enough.
